ui_training.scientific_density_modeling_requires_con: Scientific density modeling requires constant, standardized observer effort.
ui_training.maintain_a_steady_walking_pace_3: Maintain a steady walking pace (~3.0 to 4.0 km/h) along the entire transect.
ui_training.keep_gps_active_continuously_start_and: Keep GPS active continuously; start and end times record the exact survey duration.
ui_training.never_deviate_off_trail_to_search: Never deviate off-trail to search behind bushes or inside private properties.
ui_training.why_must_surveyors_maintain_a_consistent: Why must surveyors maintain a consistent walking pace without searching off-trail?
ui_training.to_maximize_the_sheer_quantity_of: To maximize the sheer quantity of animals spotted in the neighborhood
ui_training.to_ensure_standardized_observer_effort_p: To ensure standardized observer effort per unit of distance for statistical density estimation
ui_training.to_minimize_mobile_phone_battery_consump: To minimize mobile phone battery consumption during GPS tracking
ui_training.consistent_pace_standardizes_the_detecti: A steady pace keeps the detection probability g(x) comparable across time and space, so researchers can analyse the data reliably.
ui_training.distance_sampling_relies_on_the_90: Distance Sampling relies on the 90° perpendicular offset from the transect line.
ui_training.perpendicular_distance_is_the_shortest_d: Perpendicular distance is the shortest distance from the centerline to the initial animal location.
ui_training.record_the_animal_location_at_the: Record the animal location at the exact instant of first detection, before it moves.
ui_training.detection_directly_on_the_centerline_is: Detection directly on the centerline is assumed to be certain: g(0) = 1.0.
ui_training.which_distance_measurement_is_mathematic: Which distance measurement is mathematically required for Distance Sampling models?
ui_training.the_straight_line_diagonal_distance_from: The straight-line diagonal distance from the observer when first spotted
ui_training.the_90_degree_perpendicular_distance_fro: The 90-degree perpendicular distance from the transect path centerline to the animal
ui_training.the_distance_the_animal_runs_away: The distance the animal runs away after noticing the observer
ui_training.distance_sampling_specifically_integrate: Distance Sampling specifically integrates the perpendicular distance distribution to model how detection probability decays away from the line.
ui_training.a_validated_5_point_visual_scale: A validated 5-point visual scale assessing animal nutritional and welfare state.
ui_training.score_1_emaciated_ribs_lumbar_vertebrae: Score 1 (Emaciated): Ribs, lumbar vertebrae, and pelvic bones visibly prominent.
ui_training.score_2_thin_ribs_easily_visible: Score 2 (Thin): Ribs easily visible; distinct waist hourglass silhouette.
ui_training.score_3_ideal_ribs_easily_palpable: Score 3 (Ideal): Ribs easily palpable with light fat cover; well-proportioned body.
ui_training.score_4_overweight_heavy_fat_cover: Score 4 (Overweight): Heavy fat cover along lumbar vertebrae and base of tail.
ui_training.score_5_obese_distended_abdomen_with: Score 5 (Obese): Distended abdomen with heavy subcutaneous fat deposits.
ui_training.an_adult_dog_has_easily_visible: An adult dog has easily visible ribs and an hourglass waist, but lumbar spine bones do not severely protrude. What is the ICAM score?
ui_training.score_2_indicates_a_thin_animal: Score 2 indicates a thin animal with easily visible ribs and waist indentation, without the severe muscle wasting and bone protrusion of Score 1.
ui_training.note_ear_tipping_a_straight_horizontal: Note ear-tipping: a straight horizontal tip notch on the left ear indicates a sterilized animal (TNR).
ui_training.in_population_ecology_recording_zero_ani: In population ecology, recording zero animals is just as valuable as recording fifty.
ui_training.if_you_walk_2_km_along: If you walk 2 km along a transect and see no animals, keep the survey.
ui_training.confirm_yes_on_the_final_complete: Confirm "Yes" on the final complete checklist: you searched and saw zero animals.
ui_training.non_detection_data_is_the_mathematical: Non-detection data is the mathematical foundation for Occupancy and N-mixture models.
ui_training.you_walked_a_2_5_km: You walked a 2.5 km transect for 40 minutes and saw zero cats and zero dogs. What should you do?
ui_training.delete_the_session_because_an_empty: Delete the session because an empty survey contains no useful data
ui_training.invent_at_least_one_sighting_nearby: Invent at least one sighting nearby to ensure you earn experience points
ui_training.save_the_session_and_confirm_yes: Save the session and confirm "Yes" to the complete checklist (Non-detection)
ui_training.non_detections_establish_the_absence_pro: Non-detections establish the absence probability in statistical models. In Strayo, complete zero-count surveys receive full effort XP (+20 XP completion bonus) with zero penalty.
ui_training.full_completion_xp_awarded_for_zero: Full completion XP awarded for zero counts

ui_auth_v3.title: Strayo
ui_auth_v3.subtitle: Count the cats and dogs in your streets. Your walks become data researchers can use.
ui_auth_v3.have_account: Already have an account? Sign in
ui_auth_v3.privacy: Your exact locations are only shared with signed-in volunteers and researchers. Public maps show a 1 km grid.
ui_auth_v3.welcome_title: Count the cats and dogs on your street
ui_auth_v3.welcome_body: Walk, record what you see, and help researchers understand the animals that share our cities. Zero counts matter too.
ui_auth_v3.scene: A street dog and a street cat looking up

ui_consent_v3.p1_body: You help researchers understand the cats and dogs living on the streets, with a phone and a walk.
ui_consent_v3.p1_a_body: Saw a cat or dog? One photo and a count, about 20 seconds.
ui_consent_v3.p1_b_body: Walk a route and record every animal you see. This is the data science needs most.
ui_consent_v3.p1_c_body: A walk with no animals is a real result. Always finish and submit it.
ui_consent_v3.p1_d_body: Earn XP, badges and streaks for distance, time and complete walks, never for counting more animals.
ui_consent_v3.p2_body: Please read this before you start.
ui_consent_v3.p2_a_body: Never chase, corner, feed or handle an animal to get a photo or a count.
ui_consent_v3.p2_b_body: Do not photograph people, faces, number plates or private property.
ui_consent_v3.p2_c_body: Exact positions are shared only with signed-in volunteers and researchers. Public maps show a 1 km grid.
ui_consent_v3.p2_d_body: Export everything you submitted or delete your account at any time in Settings.
ui_consent_v3.agree: I agree to observe without disturbing animals or people, and to share my records for research.
ui_consent_v3.p3_body: Allow these so your records carry a position and a photo. You can change them later in Settings.
ui_consent_v3.loc_body: Places each sighting where you saw it.
ui_consent_v3.bg_body: Keeps drawing your route if the screen turns off.
ui_consent_v3.cam_body: For the optional photo of each sighting.

ui_training_v3.photo_sub: A single clear photo lets researchers recognise the same animal later.
ui_training_v3.photo_1: Take the photo side-on, so the whole body and coat pattern are visible.
ui_training_v3.photo_2: One photo per sighting is enough. Keep your distance and never approach to get closer.
ui_training_v3.photo_q: What makes the most useful photo of a street cat?
ui_training_v3.photo_q_a: A close-up of the face, taken by approaching slowly
ui_training_v3.photo_q_b: A clear side view of the whole body, taken from where you stand
ui_training_v3.photo_q_c: Several blurry photos from different angles
ui_training_v3.photo_q_expl: Coat patterns are clearest from the side, and staying where you are keeps the animal calm and you safe.
ui_training_v3.zero_badge: Counts towards the Honest zero badge
ui_training_v3.done_body: You finished all five lessons. You know how to walk a survey, judge distance and condition, take a useful photo and record zero counts.
